text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Social Democrat opposition leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa urged Prime Minister Antonio Guterres to resign and call early elections, and said his party would not give up its proposals to reform local government financing.
- The joint venture between Portugal Telecom and Brazil's Telebras, the Atlantic Alliance, seeks to invest in Portuguese- speaking African countries, Latin America and the Far East.
- Today is the deadline to deliver proposals to buy state chemicals company Quimigal Holding. The candidates are Fertigest and a consortium formed by the Mello group and Belgian manure company Sapec.
- Caldeira Dias, chairman of the Professional Training and Employment Institute, says about 80,000 people enrolled for the unemployment subsidy are not in fact unemployed.
- According to the National Statistics Institute, business activity in the industrial sector slowed down in March and employment levels in industry continued to fall.
- Portuguese railway CP has reached an agreement with Spanish railway company Renfe to launch a European group to improve railway transport between Madrid and Lisbon.

- Portugal could lose to Canada a five billion escudos investment project to build a light aircraft factory in Evora in southern Portugal due to a lack of response from Portuguese authorities to the plan.
